title: Five More Protons, Same Size: Radius and Ionisation Enthalpy across the 3d Series
subject: Chemistry
objective: Across the 3d series each new electron enters the inner (n−1)d subshell and shields the outer 4s electrons, nearly cancelling the extra nuclear charge. So atomic radii change only slightly and the first ionisation enthalpy rises slowly (631 → 906 kJ/mol), unlike across a normal period.

fill.q: Across the 3d series the added electron enters the inner ____ subshell.
Inner d electrons ____ the outer 4s electrons from the added nuclear charge.
The highest first ionisation enthalpy in the 3d series is shown by ____.
Zr and Hf have nearly equal radii because of ____ contraction.

tf.q: Atomic radii change sharply across the 3d series.
The first IE of Zn is higher than that of Sc.
Across period 3 the first IE roughly triples.

ar.a: Radii change only slightly across a transition series.
ar.r: The added electrons enter the inner (n−1)d subshell and shield the outer electrons.

ar.a: Zinc has a high first ionisation enthalpy.
ar.r: Zinc is a liquid at room temperature.
ar.explain: A true; R false: mercury is the liquid; zinc's IE is high because 3d¹⁰ 4s² is stable.

mcq.explain: Shielding nearly balances the extra charge.

num.q: By how many kJ/mol does the first IE rise from Sc (631) to Zn (906)?

short.q: Why does the first IE rise much more across period 3 than across the 3d series?
short.solution: In period 3 the added electrons enter the same outer shell and shield poorly, so the pull grows fast; in the 3d series they enter the inner 3d and shield the outer 4s.
